turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I can’t stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. I feel like people at the warehouse, or when I go salsa dancing, are noticing it all the time, even though they tell me they don’t see anything.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with a perceived crooked or 'messed up' appearance of the left side of their face despite others saying they do not notice it.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you ever consider that your face might actually look normal and this might be in your head, or are you completely certain that the deformity is real?
turns.patient_response: I mean, people keep telling me they don’t see it, so I guess part of me wonders. But it really looks crooked to me. I can’t stop focusing on the left side of my face, and it feels like people at work or salsa night have to notice it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent focus on a perceived crookedness of the left side of their face and believes others may notice it despite reassurance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself frequently checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I keep checking in the bathroom mirror. I’ll fix my cap and rub at the same spot on my face over and over. Sometimes I get so caught up doing that I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind. My boss has gotten on me about it.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeatedly checking their face in the bathroom mirror, adjusting their cap, and rubbing the same facial spot, with resulting work impairment.
